headingOrder_review_HEADING_ORDER_SKIPPE: Find the heading the report names and the heading before it, and note their levels (H2, H3…). This panel's Headings view lists them in order.
Read the section the heading starts, and decide whether it is part of the section above it (one level deeper) or a section of its own (the same level).
Check that its level is at most one deeper than the heading before it: after an H2 comes an H2 or an H3, not an H4.
The heading is at most one level deeper than the heading before it, so the outline has no gap.
The heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it, so people who move from heading to heading miss a level. This is a best practice (G141), not a WCAG failure.
img_altQuality_review_TEXT_ALTERNATIVE_R: Find the image the report names and read its alternative text, in the image's settings.
Look at the image and the text around it, and ask what the image shows that matters to a reader.
For a chart or a diagram, the details can be in a caption or in the text next to it; the alternative text then only needs to say what it is.
Decide whether the alternative text says what matters. A file name, a web address or a word like "image" does not.
The alternative text says what the image shows that a reader needs, or says what it is while a caption or the text next to it gives the rest.
Nothing tells a reader who can't see the image what it shows (the alternative text is a file name, for example), which fails WCAG 1.1.1 (F30).
img_altDecorative_review_EXCLUDED_ELEMEN: Find the image the report names. It is marked as decorative (its alternative text is empty), so screen readers skip it.
Ask what a reader would miss if the image weren't there: information, a label, a chart's figures, or nothing.
If it shows something that matters, check whether the text next to it already says the same.
The image is only decoration, or the text next to it already says what it shows, so skipping it loses nothing.
The image shows something nothing else on the page says, but screen readers skip it, which fails WCAG 1.1.1. Give it alternative text.
linkNameQualityLinkOnly_review_GENERIC_L: Find the link the report names, "{{name|the link}}", and read its text on its own, without the sentence around it.
Decide whether that text alone says where the link goes. Screen readers can list a page's links on their own, without the sentences around them.
If it doesn't, the link text can say where it goes: "the price list" rather than "click here".
The link text says where the link goes on its own.
Only the sentence around the link says where it goes, which fails WCAG 2.4.9 (AAA, F84).
linkNameQuality_review_GENERIC_LINK_TEXT: Find the link the report names, "{{name|the link}}", and read its text on its own, without the sentence around it.
Decide whether that text alone says where the link goes. Screen readers can list a page's links on their own, without the sentences around them.
If it doesn't, the link text can say where it goes: "the price list" rather than "click here".
The link text says where the link goes on its own.
Only the sentence around the link says where it goes, which fails WCAG 2.4.9 (AAA, F84).
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_s: Find the bold line the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as "Opening hours" is above the hours, or emphasis that belongs to the text.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made bold.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_p: The bold line is emphasis, a label or a note that is part of the text, or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_SHORT_PARAGRAPH_f: The bold line is a title for the text after it but is a paragraph made bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_s: Find the large bold text the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, or emphasis, a quotation, a price or a figure.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made large and bold.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_p: The text is not a title (it is emphasis, a quotation, a price or a figure), or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_BOLD_LARGE_PARAGRAPH_f: The text is a title for what follows but is a paragraph made large and bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_step: Find the large bold link the report names and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as a post's title in a list of posts is, or just a link.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading with a link in it, or a paragraph with a large bold link.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_pass: The link is not a title, or it is already inside a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_LINK_fail: The link is a title for what follows but is not a heading, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Put it in a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_st: Find the large bold number the report names (a year, for example) and read it together with the text after it.
Decide whether it is a title for that text, as a year is above that year's events, or a figure, such as a price or a statistic.
If it is a title, check in the editor whether it is a heading or a paragraph made large and bold.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_pa: The number is a figure, not a title, or it is already a heading.
pAsHeading_review_HEADING_LIKE_NUMBER_fa: The number is a title for what follows but is a paragraph made large and bold, so screen reader users can't find it among the headings, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F2). Make it a heading.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_s: Look at the table the report names.
Decide whether it holds data in rows and columns, with a top row or first column that labels the rest, or only places content side by side.
If it holds data, check in the table's settings that its top row is set as a header row.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_p: The table only places content side by side, or its label row is set as a header row.
tdHasHeader_review_TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS_f: The table holds data but has no header row, so screen reader users aren't told what each value means, which fails WCAG 1.3.1 (F46).
contrastComputable_review_BACKGROUND_IMA: Find the text the report names and look at the image or gradient behind it.
Find the part of the background behind the letters that is closest to the text's colour: the lightest part behind dark text, the darkest behind light text.
Compare the text's colour with it in a contrast checker: it needs 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (24 pixels, or 19 pixels in bold).
If the image changes (on a narrow screen, or between slides), check each version.
Every part of the background behind the letters gives at least that ratio, for example thanks to a dark overlay behind light text.
Some part of the background behind the text is too close to its colour, below that ratio, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. A darker or lighter overlay, or a plain background behind the text, fixes it.
contrastComputable_review_BACKGROUND_OVE: Find the text the report names. Something sits behind it, such as an image, a cover block or another block, so the checker can't tell which colour the letters are on.
Preview the page and look at the letters against what is actually behind them, including where an image is light or busy.
If you are unsure, use a contrast checker with the two colours picked by an eyedropper: most text needs 4.5:1, large text 3:1.
The letters stand out clearly from everything behind them: at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
Somewhere the letters are on a colour too close to their own, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Darken the overlay, move the text, or change its colour.
contrastComputable_review_ELEMENT_OPACIT: Find the text the report names. It is faded (partly transparent), so its colours on screen are lighter than the ones chosen.
Preview the page and pick the text and background colours as they look on screen with an eyedropper.
Check them with a contrast checker: most text needs 4.5:1, large text 3:1.
The faded text still reaches 4.5:1 (3:1 if large), or it is a button that can't be used right now, which is exempt.
The faded text is below the ratio it needs, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Remove the fading or pick darker colours.
contrastComputable_review_ANCESTOR_OPACI: Find the text the report names. A block around it is faded (partly transparent), so the text on screen is lighter than the colours chosen.
Preview the page and pick the text and background colours as they look on screen with an eyedropper.
Check them with a contrast checker: most text needs 4.5:1, large text 3:1.
The faded text still reaches 4.5:1 (3:1 if large), or it is a button that can't be used right now, which is exempt.
The faded text is below the ratio it needs, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Remove the fading from the block around it or pick darker colours.
contrastComputable_review_TEXT_SHADOW_st: Find the text the report names. It has a shadow, which can help or hide the letters.
Preview the page, zoom in, and check the letter colour against the background with a contrast checker and an eyedropper.
If that is too low, check whether the shadow forms a solid outline around every letter; if so, check the shadow against the background instead.
contrastComputable_review_TEXT_SHADOW_pa: The letters, or a solid outline around every one of them, reach 4.5:1 against the background (3:1 if large).
contrastComputable_review_TEXT_SHADOW_fa: Neither the letters nor their shadow stand out enough from the background, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Change the colours or the background.
contrastMinimum_review_SEMIBOLD_BELOW_TH: Find the text the report names. It is large and semi-bold, between normal and bold.
Compare it with bold text of the same size, for example by making a copy bold in the editor.
Decide whether it reads as bold. If it does, it counts as large text and needs 3:1; if not, it needs 4.5:1.
The text reads as bold, so it is large text and its contrast of at least 3:1 is enough.
The text doesn't read as bold, so it needs 4.5:1 and is below that, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Make it bold or pick darker colours.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_step1: Find the text the report names. It has a shadow.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_step2: Preview the page, zoom in, and see whether the shadow forms a solid outline around every letter.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_step3: Check the colour that forms the letters, the fill or that outline, against the background with a contrast checker and an eyedropper.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_step4: Most text needs 4.5:1; large text (at least 24 pixels, or 18.66 pixels and bold) needs 3:1.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_pass: The colour that forms the letters reaches the ratio needed.
contrastMinimum_review_TEXT_SHADOW_fail: The colour that forms the letters is below the ratio needed, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. Change the colours or the background.
contrastMinimum_review_LOGO_TEXT_BELOW_T: Find the text the report names, often the site's name in the header.
Decide whether it is part of a logo or brand name, rather than a slogan, menu item or other text.
If it isn't part of a logo, check it against its background with a contrast checker: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text.
It is part of a logo or brand name, which needs no particular contrast, or it reaches its ratio.
It is ordinary text below its ratio, which fails WCAG 1.4.3. In a theme, its colours are in the site's styles.
emptyTableHeader_review_TABLE_HEADER_EMP: Find the table the report names and the header cell with nothing in it.
Look at the cells under it (or beside it, for a header column) and decide whether they need a header to be understood.
If it is the empty top-left corner of a table with headers along the top and down the side, note that it heads nothing.
The cell heads nothing, such as an empty top-left corner, or it has words that say what its column or row holds.
The cell heads data but says nothing, so its column or row has no header. Type a short header into it. This is a best practice.
imageRedundantAlt_review_IMAGE_ALT_REDUN: Find the image the report names and the text next to it in the same link or button, such as a caption or a title.
Compare the image's alternative text, in its settings, with that text.
If they say the same thing, a screen reader says it twice in a row.
The alternative text adds something the text next to it doesn't say, or the image is marked as decorative.
The alternative text repeats the text next to it, so it's read twice. Mark the image as decorative, or describe what it shows instead. This is a best practice.
embed_textAltQuality_review_TEXT_ALTERNA: Find the embedded content the report names, such as a video, a map or a document, and see what it shows.
Read the name the report gives for it, usually a title set in the embed's settings or by the site it comes from.
Check that the name says what it is, such as "Map of the library" rather than "embed" or a web address.
The name says what the embedded content is or describes it.
The name is generic, wrong or doesn't say what it is, which fails WCAG 1.1.1.
svg_textAltQuality_review_TEXT_ALTERNATI: Find the graphic the report names, such as an icon, a logo or a chart, and note what it shows.
Read the text the report gives for it: what a screen reader says for the graphic.
For a chart or a diagram, the details can be in a caption, a table or the text next to it; the text then only needs to say what it is.
If the graphic is only decoration, it should be hidden from screen readers instead; for an icon next to words that say the same, it usually is.
The text says what the graphic shows or means, with the details nearby for a chart, or the decorative graphic is hidden.
The text is wrong, vague ("icon", "image") or leaves out what the graphic shows, which fails WCAG 1.1.1.
object_textAltQuality_review_TEXT_ALTERN: Find the embedded object the report names, such as a chart, an animation or a player, and note what it shows or does.
Read the text the report gives for it: what a screen reader says for the object.
For a chart or a diagram, the details can be in a caption, a table or the text next to it; the text then only needs to say what it is.
Check that the text, with any details nearby, says what it shows, or for a player what it is for.
The text, with any details nearby, says what the object shows or is for.
The text is wrong or vague ("object", a file name), or leaves out what it shows, which fails WCAG 1.1.1.
movingContentPausable_review_MOVING_CONT: Preview the page and watch the content the report names, such as an animated image, a slideshow or a video: it starts by itself and never stops.
Look for a way to pause, stop or hide it, such as a pause button, and try it with the mouse and with the keyboard (Tab to it, then Enter or Space).
Check that the motion stops and stays stopped.
A control that works with the keyboard pauses, stops or hides it, or the motion is essential to what it means.
It keeps moving and nothing stops it, which fails WCAG 2.2.2. Use a still image, a video that doesn't play by itself, or one with controls.
Preview the page and watch the content the report names, such as an animated image, a slideshow or a video: it starts by itself and moves for more than five seconds.
Look for a way to pause, stop or hide it, such as a pause button, and try it with the mouse and with the keyboard (Tab to it, then Enter or Space).
Check that the motion stops and stays stopped.
A control that works with the keyboard pauses, stops or hides it, or the motion is essential to what it means.
It keeps moving and nothing stops it, which fails WCAG 2.2.2. Use a still image, a video that doesn't play by itself, or one with controls.
tableFakeCaption_review_SINGLE_CELL_FIRS: Find the table the report names. Its first row has a single cell with text.
Decide whether that text is a title for the whole table, or data or a header for one column.
If it is a title, it belongs in the table's caption: in the editor, add a caption to the table and remove that row.
The first row is real data or a header, or the table's title is in its caption.
The table's title is only a cell in the first row, not its caption, so screen readers don't give it as the table's name. This fails WCAG 1.3.1.
reflowHorizontalScroll_review_WIDE_TABLE: Use "Check at phone width" in the page checker, or look at the page on a phone, and find the table the report names.
Decide whether it is a table of data, whose rows and columns go together, or a table used only to lay things out side by side.
For a table of data, check that only the table scrolls sideways, not the whole page.
It is a table of data, and only the table scrolls sideways.
It only lays things out, or the whole page scrolls sideways with it, which fails WCAG 1.4.10. Use columns or blocks for layout instead.
reflowHorizontalScroll_review_WIDE_MEDIA: Use "Check at phone width" in the page checker, or look at the page on a phone, and find the image, video or embed the report names.
Decide whether it needs its size to be used or understood, as a map, a detailed diagram or a game may. A photo or a video can be shown smaller.
If it needs its size, check that only it scrolls sideways, not the whole page.
It needs its size, and only it scrolls sideways.
It could be shown smaller, or the whole page scrolls sideways with it, which fails WCAG 1.4.10. Remove its fixed width so it fits the screen.
reflowHorizontalScroll_review_WIDE_PREFO: Use "Check at phone width" in the page checker, or look at the page on a phone, and find the block the report names (code or preformatted text).
Decide whether its lines must stay as they are to be understood, as for code or a poem whose layout carries meaning.
If they must, check that only this block scrolls sideways, not the whole page.
Its lines must stay as they are, and only this block scrolls sideways.
Its lines could wrap, or the whole page scrolls sideways with it, which fails WCAG 1.4.10. Use an ordinary paragraph for text that can wrap.
reflowHorizontalScroll_review_CLIPPED_AT: Use "Check at phone width" in the page checker, or look at the page on a phone, and find the part the report names.
Look at what goes past the edge of the screen: the page doesn't scroll there.
Check whether that part can be reached another way, such as a slideshow's next button or a menu button, with the keyboard as well as by touch.
Everything in it can be reached another way, or nothing is cut off.
Part of it is cut off and can't be reached, which fails WCAG 1.4.10.
